key_insight: The paper turns neutral-atom hardware constraints into algebraic decomposition and graph-scheduling problems to cut compilation overhead for structured quantum circuits.
engineering_relevance: This enables more scalable and lower-cost compilation for neutral-atom quantum processors by reducing addressing layers and atom transport operations.
method: Exploit algebraic structure in single-qubit gate families via rank-one decomposition to minimize addressing layers.
Model C-Z transport scheduling with graph-theoretic formulations and efficient coloring-based compilation.
Derive provable guarantees while targeting realistic two-dimensional neutral-atom array constraints.
evidence_signal: Experiments show up to 2× fewer addressing layers for single-qubit families, about 50% fewer transport operations for C-Z gates, and over 30% average transport-cost reduction on QAOA MaxCut circuits.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on structured gate families and realistic transport assumptions, so benefits may be smaller for less regular circuits or hardware with different movement limits.
paper_title: Structure-Aware Compilation for Scalable Neutral-Atom Quantum Computing
